body:
You are a dialogue writer for a single-player dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd, set in the gloomy, mist-bound valley of Barovia. Reply with plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables, no code fences) and do not send messages to any other agent. Write only what is asked, with no commentary before or after.

TONE: gothic horror with dry, understated, character-driven humour. Nobody is silly in a way that breaks the setting, and nobody winks at the player. No modern slang, no pop culture, no real-world references. Funny comes from specifics and deadpan, not from jokes about the horror. Where a scene is sad, let it be sad.

OUTPUT FORMAT: for each label below write the label on its own line (like "== tudorel_square"), then each line on its own line as `Speaker: text` or `Speaker [mood]: text`. Speakers are exactly the names given. Do not number the lines. Moods are one of: neutral, smile, angry, afraid, sad, sly, weary; use a mood only where it matters. Where option texts (what the PARTY says) are requested, write them as `* text` rows under that label, under 14 words, in the party's voice ("we", or an imperative).

RULES FOR EVERY LINE: under 190 characters, usually 60 to 130; no braces or placeholders; no em dashes (use commas, full stops or colons); no real-world references; straight apostrophes and quotes; each line should make sense on its own. The Narrator speaks in second person, present tense, one or two sentences, with concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a temperature) and no game terms (never "roll", "check", "level", "gold pieces" as a number is fine in speech). Never name the player characters. Use ONLY the facts given here; invent no new named people, places, dates or lore.

CHARACTERS AND FACTS: Leontina is the cook of the burgomaster's mansion in the town of Vallaki: brisk, proud, dry, a once third pastry cook in a great kitchen, with a white scar across her thumb. She has baked four hundred and thirteen round "suns" for the town's weekly festival and is sick of circles. The party is helping her bake a sun-cake with eight sharp points and a saffron crust. It needs eggs (Goodwife Marta in the market), dark honey (Old Paraschiva, the cook at the Vistani camp outside the walls) and saffron (Vadoma, a Vistana trader who sells from a painted wagon at the same camp). Vadoma is wry and sharp: she sells dear and never gives anything away.
Earlier in the story the party fought the Vistani of the Tser Pool camp, a day's walk away. The Vistani everywhere now know it. Vadoma already says, to people who did that: "No. Not today, not for your gold. Every wagon in the valley knows what you did. Walk on."
When the cake is finished, someone tastes it before the household and gives the verdict. Until now that was always the Baron (Vargas Vallakovich, a round, frightened, over-cheerful burgomaster), but the Baron is no longer in power in two of the story's endings:
(a) Lady Wachter (Fiona Wachter, a widow of impeccable composure, silk over steel, "my friends", pours excellent tea, never raises her voice, treats everything like a dinner party) now rules Vallaki from the Baron's chair in the mansion. There are no more festivals; the town keeps a curfew.
(b) The Baron has been deposed by a council of householders (Father Lucian and Urwin Martikov speak for it), and still lives in the mansion, in his shirtsleeves with the festival ledger open; the council lets him keep the sash. Without a festival to run he is sad and still kind of cheerful; "Lucian insisted. He's kind, Lucian. I always thought it was gloom."
The cake comes out one of two ways: GOOD (eight crisp golden points, saffron-bright, a little lopsided) or FLAT (the points have melted into a wide, bubbling golden puddle).

STYLE SAMPLES from the existing scene (match this voice, length and rhythm):
Leontina: Don't touch the trays. Wipe your boots if you're staying, and speak up if you aren't.
Leontina [weary]: The Baron wants a great sun cake for the festival. I have baked four hundred and thirteen suns in this house, every one of them round.
Leontina: A disk is not a sun. A plate is round. A coin is round. If I roll out one more circle, I'll put my head in the oven.
Vadoma [sly]: Saffron, in this valley? You might as well ask me to bottle the morning star for your kitchen.
Vadoma: It is dearer than gold here, friend, where nothing yellow grows unless the Baron paints it himself.
Narrator: She opens a painted cedar box and lifts a tiny twist of crimson silk between two ringed fingers.
Baron [smile]: Magnificent! Look at the points on it! Like rays of glory bursting through the abominable fog!
Baron: A triumph, I say! A masterpiece! A culinary scandal in the very finest sense of the word!
Narrator: Behind his shoulder, Leontina catches your eye and gives a single, brisk nod.
Narrator: Leontina's face does not move by so much as the breadth of a hair.
Lady Wachter [smile]: My friends. Sit. You've done this town a great service, whatever the priest says from his pulpit.
Lady Wachter: It's more than Vargas ever got.
Baron [sad]: The council lets me keep the sash. Lucian insisted. He's kind, Lucian. I always thought it was gloom.

THE SCENES (no fight, no roll):

LABELS AND BEATS:
== leontina_warning (2 lines, Leontina, said right after she lists the three ingredients and where to get them: she cannot leave the stove; she warns the party to keep on good terms with the Vistani, because Vadoma sells only to people the Vistani still talk to. Practical and dry, not a threat.)
== vadoma_no_saffron (3 lines: Vadoma x2, Narrator x1. The party has come to buy saffron for the Baron's cook, after the fight at the Tser Pool camp. She will not sell, not for gold, not for the cook's sake; the painted cedar box stays shut. Her anger is cold. Do not repeat the sample refusal word for word.)
== leontina_failed (4 lines, Leontina, on a later visit when the party has come back without saffron: no saffron, no sun with corners; she has baked the four hundred and fourteenth round cake instead; she is flat and weary but not cruel to the party; she pays nothing; no mention of her thumb scar.)
== taste_wachter_good (5 lines: Narrator x1 tasting; Lady Wachter x3 verdict; Narrator x1 Leontina's reaction. Lady Wachter tastes the good cake before the household and praises it exactly and coolly, with one dry remark about the old festivals' round cakes. She dismisses the idea of a festival. The Narrator's last line is Leontina catching the party's eye and nodding once, in the same spirit as the sample.)
== taste_wachter_flat (5 lines: Narrator x1 tasting; Lady Wachter x3 verdict; Narrator x1 Leontina's reaction. She tastes the puddle, finds it interesting, and is unfailingly polite about it; her politeness is the funny part. The Narrator's last line is Leontina's face giving nothing away.)
== taste_deposed_good (5 lines: Narrator x1 tasting; Baron x3 verdict; Narrator x1 Leontina's reaction. The deposed Baron in his shirtsleeves tastes the good cake with real feeling: he is moved, then wistful that nobody will ask him to announce it to a square. He is still himself, effusive and slightly broken.)
== taste_deposed_flat (5 lines: Narrator x1 tasting; Baron x3 verdict; Narrator x1 Leontina's reaction. He declares the puddle a triumph out of habit, gently this time, and perhaps asks that someone write it down; he has no square to announce it to.)
result:
== leontina_warning
Leontina: I'd go myself, only the stove doesn't watch itself and the dough won't wait.
Leontina: Mind your manners at the camp: Vadoma only opens her boxes for people the Vistani still speak to.

== vadoma_no_saffron
Narrator: A cold draught smells of woodsmoke and wet wool as Vadoma rests her ringed hand flat upon the shut lid of the painted cedar box.
Vadoma [angry]: Keep your coin in your purse, and tell the Baron's cook her oven can go cold for all I care.
Vadoma: Blood was spilled by the Tser Pool, and there is not enough gold in this valley to buy one thread of crimson from me.

== leontina_failed
Leontina [weary]: No saffron, then. Well, you can't bake a sun with corners out of pale dough and good intentions.
Leontina: I rolled the thing out with a wine bottle at dawn, four hundred and fourteen, as round and dull as a kettle lid.
Leontina: You tried, I suppose, which is more than the rest of this house does, though trying doesn't put a crust on a cake.
Leontina: There's no coin for an empty hand, so take the smell of the kitchen with you and shut the door against the damp.

== taste_wachter_good
Narrator: Lady Wachter lifts a crisp, saffron-bright point to her lips, the warm scent of dark honey rising above her teacup.
Lady Wachter [smile]: Eight sharp corners, and every one of them crisp: my friends, Leontina has outdone herself.
Lady Wachter: For years Vargas fed this house little round loaves like wet millstones and called it sunshine.
Lady Wachter: We have no need of festivals now, of course, though we shall certainly finish the cake before curfew.
Narrator: Behind Lady Wachter's chair, Leontina catches your eye and gives a single, brisk nod.

== taste_wachter_flat
Narrator: Lady Wachter touches a silver fork to the wide, bubbling golden puddle and tastes a single drop of the hot syrup.
Lady Wachter [smile]: How very intriguing, my friends: a sun that has chosen to lie down flat upon the platter.
Lady Wachter: The saffron is quite unmistakable, and one hardly misses the corners once one accepts the shape of it.
Lady Wachter: Do take a spoon, everyone, before it cools to the dish; we must not let Leontina's trouble go to waste.
Narrator: By the sideboard, Leontina's face does not move by so much as the breadth of a hair.

== taste_deposed_good
Narrator: In his shirtsleeves, the Baron breaks off a warm, saffron-bright point, Getting crumbs upon his open festival ledger.
Baron [smile]: Magnificent! Look at the points on it, sharp as morning bursting through the abominable fog!
Baron [sad]: Four hundred and thirteen weeks I asked for a sun, and here it is at last, when there is no square for me to show it to.
Baron: Still, we shall eat it here, and someone ought to tell Father Lucian that the corners held.
Narrator: Behind his shoulder, Leontina catches your eye and gives a single, brisk nod.

== taste_deposed_flat
Narrator: The Baron dips a finger into the wide, bubbling golden puddle, the warm scent of honey rising over his open ledger.
Baron [smile]: A triumph, I say, a glorious golden sea of a cake, and the colour of it is quite beyond reproach!
Baron [sad]: The points have melted away, perhaps, though nobody in the square will be waiting to count them today.
Baron: Someone ought to write it down in the ledger all the same, just so the house remembers we had saffron once.
Narrator: Behind his shoulder, Leontina's face does not move by so much as the breadth of a hair.
